articles.title: Leafy greens versus meat: Where your nitrates come from may matter for brain health
articles.summary: Leafy greens and bacon both contain nitrates, but a large Danish study suggests the source may matter. Plant-sourced nitrate was tied to lower dementia rates, while animal and tap water nitrate was tied to higher rates.

articles.title: Oxytocin alters how the brain learns and remembers social hierarchies
articles.summary: A new study reveals how the hormone oxytocin alters the brain's ability to learn and remember social hierarchies, boosting memory for networks that do not directly involve the observer.

articles.title: Irritable kids are hard to parent, and that strain may show up years later, new study suggests
articles.summary: Do irritable kids shape their parents, or the other way around? A study following families from age 3 to 6 found links in both directions, though the stronger pattern ran from child to parent.

articles.title: Women who use social media more are more open to “sugar relationships,” especially in looser cultures
articles.summary: Women who use social media more often tend to be more open to sugar relationships, according to a study of 22,292 women in 22 countries. The link was modestly stronger in countries with looser social norms.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? articles.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden gut-to-brain dopamine pathway that helps explain why bitter coffee and other initially unpleasant flavors can become favorites over time. The discovery reveals how the brain learns to crave certain foods and could eventually lead to new ways of reshaping eating habits and food preferences.

articles.title: Common osteoporosis drugs linked to 24% lower dementia risk in major study
articles.summary: A massive study of more than 120,000 older adults suggests that common osteoporosis drugs may reduce the risk of Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias by up to 24%. The surprising findings raise the possibility that medications already used to strengthen bones could also help protect the aging brain.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden warning sign of cannabis addiction
articles.summary: A study of more than 17,700 US adults found that people who use cannabis in multiple forms have dramatically higher rates of daily consumption and addiction symptoms than those who stick primarily to one method. Nearly 67% of those who used almost every form met criteria for cannabis use disorder, compared with just 15% of people who mainly consumed edibles.

articles.title: Psychology’s tools for measuring masculinity lean heavily toward the negative, review finds
articles.summary: Is psychology only looking for problems when it studies men? A review of 50 years of masculinity scales found that 78 percent focused mainly on harms, and many overlooked culture and social context.
